text:
deploy-bot: Rolling `v3.5.2` to prod (region=eu-north). Monitors: p95, error-rate, kvcache-miss. Auto-rollback=enabled.

lina: p95 spiked +30% in eu-north within 2m, errors +2.2%. Looks localized to older hosts behind the LB.

omar: logs show repeated cache rehydration (kvcache miss storm) and transient OOMs on hostgroup eu-north-legacy. Could be mem-profile regress.

sam: our plan was to manual-pin if errors >2.5% for 15m. This hit 2.2% so deploy-bot didn't reach manual threshold. I'd prefer we hold auto-rollback and promote the mem-fix patch `v3.5.2-memhotfix` to that region. Thoughts?

ops-oncall: auto-rollback triggered at 5260001128 for eu-north due to kvcache-miss rule threshold=2.0%. Rollback started to `v3.5.1`. I can pause the automated rollback and set lock while we push the hotfix.

product: customer impact reported from one enterprise tenant in EU—notified SE. We should include an explicit note in release notes if we pin older artifact.

lina: please hold auto-rollback. I'll push `v3.5.2-memhotfix` to artifact registry now. ETA 7m.

ops-oncall: holding further auto-rollback for eu-north. Lock cmd: `redwoodctl rollout lock --region eu-north --by ops-oncall --reason "manual hold for hotfix"`

deploy-bot: Acknowledged. Auto-rollback suppressed for 20m. Will escalate on critical infra alerts.

omar: hotfix promoted and 10% canary started:
`redwoodctl promote --artifact v3.5.2-memhotfix --region eu-north --traffic 10`

sam: canary looks good after 3m: p95 back to baseline, no OOMs. Proceed to full push and then pin region to memhotfix.

ops-oncall: promoting to 100% and pinning eu-north to `v3.5.2-memhotfix` to avoid further auto-rollback churn.

product: drafting status message: "We observed a regional memory regression impacting EU-north. We rolled back the affected fleet, promoted a hotfix, and pinned the region. Some customers briefly experienced higher latency; no data loss."

lina: will follow up with postmortem and update rollback rule sensitivity. Tagging @omar for triage.

deploy-bot: Thread closed. Auto-rollback remains enabled globally except where manual locks are applied.
